_doc: Dated Planning Code controls for the pathway rules (rule table v2). Transcribed from the code text on 2026-11-10, each entry read twice (the second time blind) and settled where the readings differed; every version carries a verbatim quote and the URL read. 'from' null = already in force on 2022-01-01; 'to' null = in force today. Built by scripts/validation/assemble_dated_controls.py; do not edit by hand.

CODE TEXTS DIFFER from this date: Ord. 122-23, File No. 230371 (https://sfbos.archive.sf.gov/sites/default/files/o0122-23.pdf, p. 25; section history App. 7/5/2023, Eff. 8/5/2023; repeated in Ord. 159-23, File No. 230732, Eff. 8/28/2023) struck § 121.6(c), the prohibition over 120,000 gross sq ft, and left only the Conditional Use over 50,000 gross sq ft outside C-3, but the Table 210.1 row kept its 'NP above 120,000 gross square feet' sentence (still there in the archived copy of 17 Jan 2025, https://web.archive.org/web/20250117213838/https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/san_francisco/latest/sf_planning/0-0-0-20117). Reconciler: § 121.6 today requires the Conditional Use over 50,000 gross square feet 'unless such use already is prohibited'; it no longer states the 120,000 prohibition itself, and the Table 210.1 row still does. Neither reader resolved which text governs; the values follow the table row, as both readers have them.

settled.quote: Conditional Use Authorization is not required for such a division or for the individual resulting Non-Residential Use Sizes, provided the division does not cause a Net Addition of Gross Floor Area.
settled.reason: Ord. 173-25 added the sentence "Division of large use sizes per § 121.5." to the row. Neither reader had read § 121.5; the first recorded the pointer, the second left the exemption empty. § 121.5(a), read now, lets an existing over-size use be divided with no Conditional Use for the division or the resulting sizes where the district row cites § 121.5, as this row does. Thresholds unchanged.

(not permitted above it). § 121.4, read on the mirror (https://gocodebook.com/library/us/ca/san-francisco-planning/article-1.2-dimensions-areas-and-open-spaces/sec.-121.-minimum-lot-width-and-area/sec.-121.4.-non-residential-use-size-limits-in-mixed-use-districts; last amended by Ord. 197-21, File No. 210600, App. 11/5/2021, Eff. 12/6/2021, so the same text was in force on 1 Jan 2022): Commercial Uses over the Use Size Limit and up to the Use Size Maximum need Conditional Use; uses above the Maximum 'shall not be permitted'. use_size.note: P up to 4,000 sq ft; C 4,001 sq ft and above; no NP band, no exemption. Change read in Ord. 173-25 (https://sfbos.archive.sf.gov/sites/default/files/o0173-25.pdf, p. 26: Section 4 table, old text struck and new text added for "SEC. 711. NC-2", read on the page image because the text layer garbles the marked-up words); the section's legislative history gives App. 9/5/2025, Eff. 10/6/2025. The same ordinance (pp. 4-5) changed Section 121.2(a) so that only uses "larger than" the stated size need Conditional Use (the words "of the same size or" were struck), with "NC-2, NCT-2 ... 4,000 sq. ft." in its table. Today's row read on the gocodebook.com mirror (2026-08 edition, text as of 2026-09-23). Reconciliation (2026-11-10): the Use Size row itself prints no exemption, but Section 121.2(a), which the row cites, makes the Conditional Use requirement 'subject to the exception in Section 121.2(b)', and Section 121.2(b) as it reads today on the mirror lets an existing Non-Residential Use larger than the limit be divided into smaller ones that are still larger than the limit without Conditional Use if there is no Net Addition of Gross Floor Area. The mirror's history for Section 121.2 reads 'new divisions (b) and (d) added; Ord. 173-25, Eff. 10/6/2025' and 'divisions (b), (c), and (d) amended; Ord. 13-26, Eff. 3/16/2026'; the wording of division (b) between 2025-10-06 and 2026-03-15 was not read by the reconciler (the ordinance files exceed the fetch size limit); the second reader read it in Ord. 173-25, pp. 4-7. A new use above the threshold still needs Conditional Use; this exception is only for dividing an existing over-size use. The second reading also notes that Ord. 245-25 (Eff. 1/12/2026) reprints the table with the old wording as unchanged text; the mirror carries the new wording quoted here. Today's Use Size row was re-read on the mirror on 2026-11-10 and reads as quoted.

formula_retail.note: Table 833: P(3). Note 3: 'For projects within the Central SoMa SUD, see specific requirements in Section 249.78.' Inside the Central SoMa SUD, § 249.78 (https://gocodebook.com/library/us/ca/san-francisco-planning/article-6/sec.-249.78.-central-soma-special-use-district) says Formula Retail uses that are also Bar, Restaurant or Limited Restaurant uses 'shall not be permitted', and § 303.1 today (https://gocodebook.com/library/us/ca/san-francisco-planning/article-3-zoning-procedures/sec.-303.-conditional-uses/sec.-303.1.-formula-retail-uses) requires a Conditional Use for Formula Retail in the 'Central SoMa Special Use District (Sec. 249.78)' ((e)(4)) and lists Formula Retail Bar, Restaurant and Limited Restaurant uses as not permitted there ((f)(4)(A)). So the rewrite turned 'Elsewhere, C for all Formula Retail Uses' into P outside the Central SoMa SUD: a change of permission made by a reorganising ordinance, worth a second reading. outdoor_activity_area.note: NA: Table 827 has no Outdoor Activity Area row in any copy read. Compared the archived codelibrary.amlegal.com copies of 22 Oct 2021 (https://web.archive.org/web/20211022013923/https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/san_francisco/latest/sf_planning/0-0-0-26847), 10 Jun 2023 (https://web.archive.org/web/20230610015354/https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/san_francisco/latest/sf_planning/0-0-0-26847) and 26 Jun 2024 (https://web.archive.org/web/20240626122554/https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/san_francisco/latest/sf_planning/0-0-0-26847) with the gocodebook.com mirror (2026-08 edition, text as of 2026-09-23). What governs instead: row .26, 'All Non-Residential Uses Permitted, except as described below', and nothing below it restricts an outdoor activity area; § 825(c)(1)(A) today (https://gocodebook.com/library/us/ca/san-francisco-planning/article-8-mixed-use-districts/sec.-825.-dtr-downtown-residential-districts): 'All Uses are permitted as Principal Uses as of right in a Downtown Residential district unless otherwise indicated as a Conditional Use or Not Permitted in this Section 825 or any other Section governing an individual DTR District' (its 2022 wording was not read). No rule by location and no reference to § 202.2(a)(7) was found for this district. Reconciler: 'governed_by' restates the first reader's 'what governs instead' as values (P wherever located). The second reader says the table does not separately control an outdoor activity area; same outcome. It is an inference from row .26 and § 825(c)(1)(A), not a printed cell.

rules.rule: A new Bar may be approved by Conditional Use on the First Story only if the Zoning Administrator first finds the space is currently or was last legally occupied by a Bar, that use was not discontinued or abandoned, and the new Bar will not enlarge the space. rules.note: Lead-in to (c)(1): 'Restaurant, Limited Restaurant, and Bar uses may be permitted as a Conditional Use on the First Story through the procedures set forth in Section 303 only if the Zoning Administrator first determines that the proposed new Restaurant, Limited Restaurant, or Bar would occupy a space that is currently or was last legally occupied by one of the uses described below; provided that its last use has not been discontinued or abandoned pursuant to Sections 186.1(d) or 178(d) of this Code and that the proposed new use will not enlarge the space; and provided further that no Conditional Use shall be required if the use remains the same as the prior authorized use, with no enlargement or intensification of use'. enlarge_or_intensify.rule: A permitted conditional use (one authorized by Conditional Use, one that lawfully existed when the Code first made that use conditional, or one deemed so under § 179) may continue in the form authorized or lawfully existing, but may not be significantly altered, enlarged or intensified without a new Conditional Use (§ 178(a), (b), (c)(1)). If it is discontinued for three years (18 months in the Castro Street NCD and the Jackson Square SUD, and 18 months for a conditional Formula Retail use) or otherwise abandoned, it may be restored only by a new Conditional Use (§ 178(d)). In a Neighborhood Commercial district a nonconforming use may not be significantly altered, enlarged or intensified without a Conditional Use, may not expand beyond its lot or above the storeys it lawfully occupies, and may not be re-established after three years of non-use (18 months in the North Beach, Polk Street, Castro Street and Haight Street NCDs) (§ 186.1(a), (b)(1), (d)). Outside NC districts a nonconforming use may not be enlarged, intensified, extended or moved, or extended into additional space, at all (§ 181(a)), with stated exceptions (Nighttime Entertainment in MUG and MUR by Conditional Use, § 181(f); up to 25% more gross floor area once, by Conditional Use, in the Eastern Neighborhoods Mixed Use, PDR-1-D and PDR-1-G districts, § 181(i)); it may not be changed so as to increase its degree of nonconformity (§ 182(a)) and may be changed to a use that is conditional in the district only by Conditional Use (§ 182(c)). In this period the third condition of the § 181(f) exception for Nighttime Entertainment in MUG and MUR was that 'the provisions of Section 803.5(b) of this Code are satisfied' (§ 181(f)(3)).
enlarge_or_intensify.quote: A permitted conditional use may not be significantly altered, enlarged, or intensified, except upon approval of a new conditional use application pursuant to the provisions of Article 3 of this Code.
enlarge_or_intensify.note: What the text itself says counts: the Code does not define 'significantly altered, enlarged, or intensified'. § 178(c)(2)-(4) names three cases: an Internet Services Exchange (a physical alteration that enlarges the building to intensify the use, or a larger electrical service needing a permit); Formula Retail (a change of owner or operator with one of the listed limbs, see formula_retail_definition); a Power Plant (output up more than 10%, change of fuel, and others). For a nonconforming use in an NC district, § 186.1(a) lets it expand in floor area only under (b) (that is, by Conditional Use), never beyond its lot or above the storey or storeys it lawfully occupies (except § 186.2), and § 186.1(b)(2) lets it expand onto the public sidewalk with tables and chairs. Zoning Administrator Interpretation 186.1(b), 'Nonconforming use, "significant" defined' (effective 12/88, 5/98, revised 3/21; it says § 178(c) carries the same limitation): significant enlargements are expansion of more than 25% of the floor area or more than 500 square feet, whichever is less, and expansion into an adjacent storefront that had been occupied by a nonconforming use in a different use category; a significant intensification is the exchange of an ABC Type 47 licence for a Type 48. Not significant: expansion up to 25% of the floor area or 500 square feet, whichever is less; adding kitchen equipment or menu items to an existing restaurant; exchanging a Type 42 licence for a Type 48. Kitchen floor-area expansion is case by case. This is an interpretation, not Code text; it carries no ordinance date and was read only in the copy last updated 2026-09-23. Copies compared: § 178, archived amlegal copy of 23 Dec 2021 (history ending Ord. 204-19) against the gocodebook.com mirror (2026-08 edition, text as of 2026-09-23): (a), (b), (c)(1), (c)(2), (c)(4) and (d) are word for word the same; the differences are (c)(3)(E) (deleted by Ord. 62-25, Eff. 6/1/2025, recorded under formula_retail_definition) and (e)(5)-(6) (deleted by Ord. 173-25, Eff. 10/6/2025, recorded under use_size_general). § 186.1, archived copy of 18 Aug 2022 (history ending Ord. 202-18) against the mirror: (a), (b)(1), (b)(2) and (d) the same. § 181, archived copy of 21 Jan 2022 against the mirror: (a) the same; (f) was reworded by Ord. 70-23 (Eff. 6/3/2023), which replaced 'the provisions of Section 803.5(b)' with the Entertainment Commission's Good Neighbor Policy. § 182, archived copy of 5 Aug 2021 against the mirror: identical. In this period § 186.1(b)(3) ended at 'required standards for new construction set forth in this Code', and § 186.1(c)(4)-(5) and § 178(e)(5)-(6) still made a change of use of an oversized use in the North Beach and Castro Street NCDs subject to Conditional Use. Reconciled 2026-11-10: this version now ends on 2023-06-02 because § 181(f)(3) was reworded by Ord. 70-23 (Eff. 6/3/2023); the Conditional Use requirement for altering, enlarging or intensifying did not change on that date.

enlarge_or_intensify.quote: A permitted conditional use may not be significantly altered, enlarged, or intensified, except upon approval of a new conditional use application pursuant to the provisions of Article 3 of this Code.
enlarge_or_intensify.note: What the text itself says counts: the Code does not define 'significantly altered, enlarged, or intensified'. § 178(c)(2)-(4) names three cases: an Internet Services Exchange (a physical alteration that enlarges the building to intensify the use, or a larger electrical service needing a permit); Formula Retail (a change of owner or operator with one of the listed limbs, see formula_retail_definition); a Power Plant (output up more than 10%, change of fuel, and others). For a nonconforming use in an NC district, § 186.1(a) lets it expand in floor area only under (b) (that is, by Conditional Use), never beyond its lot or above the storey or storeys it lawfully occupies (except § 186.2), and § 186.1(b)(2) lets it expand onto the public sidewalk with tables and chairs. Zoning Administrator Interpretation 186.1(b), 'Nonconforming use, "significant" defined' (effective 12/88, 5/98, revised 3/21; it says § 178(c) carries the same limitation): significant enlargements are expansion of more than 25% of the floor area or more than 500 square feet, whichever is less, and expansion into an adjacent storefront that had been occupied by a nonconforming use in a different use category; a significant intensification is the exchange of an ABC Type 47 licence for a Type 48. Not significant: expansion up to 25% of the floor area or 500 square feet, whichever is less; adding kitchen equipment or menu items to an existing restaurant; exchanging a Type 42 licence for a Type 48. Kitchen floor-area expansion is case by case. This is an interpretation, not Code text; it carries no ordinance date and was read only in the copy last updated 2026-09-23. Copies compared: § 178, archived amlegal copy of 23 Dec 2021 (history ending Ord. 204-19) against the gocodebook.com mirror (2026-08 edition, text as of 2026-09-23): (a), (b), (c)(1), (c)(2), (c)(4) and (d) are word for word the same; the differences are (c)(3)(E) (deleted by Ord. 62-25, Eff. 6/1/2025, recorded under formula_retail_definition) and (e)(5)-(6) (deleted by Ord. 173-25, Eff. 10/6/2025, recorded under use_size_general). § 186.1, archived copy of 18 Aug 2022 (history ending Ord. 202-18) against the mirror: (a), (b)(1), (b)(2) and (d) the same. § 181, archived copy of 21 Jan 2022 against the mirror: (a) the same; (f) was reworded by Ord. 70-23 (Eff. 6/3/2023), which replaced 'the provisions of Section 803.5(b)' with the Entertainment Commission's Good Neighbor Policy. § 182, archived copy of 5 Aug 2021 against the mirror: identical. In this period § 186.1(b)(3) ended at 'required standards for new construction set forth in this Code', and § 186.1(c)(4)-(5) and § 178(e)(5)-(6) still made a change of use of an oversized use in the North Beach and Castro Street NCDs subject to Conditional Use. formula_retail_definition.rule: A Formula Retail use is a retail sales or service activity or establishment that has eleven or more other retail sales establishments in operation, or with local land use or permit entitlements already approved, anywhere in the world, and that maintains two or more of these standardised features: a standardized array of merchandise (50% or more of in-stock merchandise from a single distributor bearing uniform markings), a standardized facade, a standardized decor and color scheme, uniform apparel, standardized signage, a trademark or a servicemark (§ 303.1(b)). It applies only to the uses listed in § 303.1(c), which include Bar, Restaurant, Limited-Restaurant, Eating and Drinking Use and Liquor Store, whether principal or accessory. Establishing a Formula Retail use in any Article 7 Neighborhood Commercial district needs a Conditional Use, except where the district does not permit it at all (§ 703.4(b); § 303.1(e), (f)). In § 303.1(e) the Neighborhood Commercial item is numbered (e)(1). Change of operator: a change of owner or operator of an existing Formula Retail establishment is an intensification needing a new Conditional Use if any one of five things is true: (A) a change of use, including within Retail Sales and Service sub-categories; (B) expansion of use size; (C) the new chain has more locations than the old one; (D) installation of a commercial kitchen; (E) the existing Formula Retail use had never been authorized by a Conditional Use (§ 178(c)(3)). Otherwise the change is approved administratively under the Performance-Based Design Guidelines (§ 303.1(j)).
formula_retail_definition.kind_note: Carries both the definition and the approval rule (Conditional Use in NC districts; change of operator).

use_size_general.rule: In the NC and NCT districts listed in § 121.2(a), a Non-Residential Use of the same size as or larger than the district's figure (2,000 to 6,000 square feet by district; 10,000 in the Regional Commercial District) may be permitted only as a Conditional Use, with three extra criteria; and under § 121.2(b) a use over a hard cap (4,000 square feet in the West Portal Avenue, North Beach, Castro Street, Polk Street and Pacific Avenue NCDs; 25,000 in the Regional Commercial District) is not permitted, with listed exceptions. What triggers it: § 121.2 does not name the act. It limits the size of 'each individual Non-Residential Use', measured as Gross Floor Area, so the test is the size of the use that results: a new use at or above the figure, or an enlargement (including taking in a neighbouring storefront) that brings a use to or above it, needs a Conditional Use; mergers are not mentioned by name except lot mergers in the Mission Street NCT (§ 121.2(c)). Taking over an existing oversized space: the text is silent in general. In the North Beach NCD (any use over the § 121.2(a) or (b) figure) and the Castro Street NCD (a use over (a) but under the (b) cap) a change to a new use needed a new Conditional Use (§ 178(e)(5), (6); for nonconforming uses § 186.1(c)(4), (5)). Elsewhere the Zoning Administrator's Interpretation 121.2 (10/93) says a conforming use over the threshold that predates the limit can change to a different use in the same floor area without a Conditional Use if there is no significant increase in floor area.
use_size_general.quote: Non-Residential Uses of the same size or larger than the square footage stated in the table below may be permitted only as Conditional Uses. The use area shall be measured as the Gross Floor Area for each individual Non-Residential Use.
use_size_general.note: Text before the 2025 rewrite read in the archived amlegal copy of 27 Jan 2022 (history ending Ord. 202-18, Eff. 9/10/2018) and, as struck text, in Ord. 173-25 (https://sfbos.archive.sf.gov/sites/default/files/o0173-25.pdf). Note the threshold wording: 'of the same size or larger', so a use of exactly the figure was conditional. Amendments inside this period that did not change the general rule (per the section history on the mirror; not each read): Ord. 11-23, Eff. 3/12/2023 (divisions (b), (b)(3) and the (b) table: the Polk Street exception extended to expansion of an existing General Grocery, seen as struck text in Ord. 173-25); Ord. 169-24, Eff. 8/12/2024 (table note: no Conditional Use for a Legacy Business Limited Restaurant relocating within the Polk Street NCD); Ord. 2-25, Eff. 3/10/2025 (a Health Service use on one West Portal parcel); Ord. 23-25, Eff. 4/7/2025 ((a) table). District figures belong to each district's use_size row. The reading that the trigger is the resulting size of the use is mine from the wording; the Code has no sentence listing 'new use, enlargement, merger'.

What triggers it: § 121.2 still does not name the act. It limits 'Non-Residential Use Sizes', measured as Gross Floor Area for each individual Non-Residential Use, so the test is the size of the use that results: a new use larger than the figure, or an enlargement (including taking in a neighbouring storefront) that makes a use larger than it, needs a Conditional Use; mergers are not mentioned by name except lot mergers in the Mission Street NCT (§ 121.2(c)). Dividing an existing oversized use into two or more smaller uses, even ones still over the limit, needs no Conditional Use if there is no Net Addition of Gross Floor Area (§ 121.2(b), § 121.5). Taking over an existing oversized space: the text is silent, and the two provisions that used to require a new Conditional Use for that in North Beach and Castro Street (§ 178(e)(5)-(6), § 186.1(c)(4)-(5)) were deleted. The Zoning Administrator's Interpretation 121.2 (10/93), still published, says a conforming use over the threshold that predates the limit can change to a different use in the same floor area without a Conditional Use if there is no significant increase in floor area.

outdoor_activity_area_general.rule: Under § 145.2, in NC districts an Outdoor Activity Area operated by a Commercial Use is a Principal Use if it is outside a building and contiguous to the front property line of the lot (in NC-S districts, within the property and in front of the primary facades with customer entrances); one that does not meet that test is a Conditional Use. Under § 202.2(a)(7), an Outdoor Activity Area is principally permitted in any Neighborhood Commercial or Neighborhood Commercial Transit district if it meets all five limits: (A) on the ground level; (B) in operation only between 9:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m.; (C) not operated in association with a Bar use; (D) with a Limited Restaurant or Restaurant, seated areas only, no standing; (E) alcohol dispensed only inside or by wait staff at the patron's outdoor seat. Any Outdoor Activity Area seeking to operate beyond these limits needs a Conditional Use unless § 145.2 permits it.

outdoor_activity_area_general.rule: Under § 145.2, in NC districts an Outdoor Activity Area operated by a Commercial Use is a Principal Use if it is outside a building and contiguous to the front property line of the lot (in NC-S districts, within the property and in front of the primary facades with customer entrances); one that does not meet that test is a Conditional Use. Under § 202.2(a)(7), an Outdoor Activity Area is principally permitted in any Neighborhood Commercial or Neighborhood Commercial Transit district, and in the WMUG, WMUO, SALI and RED-MX districts, if it meets all five limits: (A) on the ground level; (B) in operation only between 9:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m.; (C) not operated in association with a Bar use; (D) with a Limited Restaurant or Restaurant, seated areas only, no standing; (E) alcohol dispensed only inside or by wait staff at the patron's outdoor seat. From this date the Conditional Use for going beyond the limits is required only of an Outdoor Activity Area that is not at the front of a building (and not otherwise permitted by § 145.2).
outdoor_activity_area_general.quote: Any Outdoor Activity Area not at the front of a building seeking to operate beyond these limitations requires a Conditional Use Authorization, unless such Outdoor Activity Area is permitted by Planning Code Section 145.2.

Whether a district's own table relies on § 202.2(a)(7) differs by district (some rows read 'P if located in front; C if located elsewhere' with no reference to it, others 'P if located in front or it complies with Section 202.2(a)(7)'); that is recorded in each district's outdoor_activity_area row, not here. The reference in § 145.2(b) to 'Paragraph 1 of this subsection (b)' is a leftover cross-reference; it is read as pointing to the front-of-lot test in (a). Ord. 85-24 (read at https://sfbos.archive.sf.gov/sites/default/files/o0085-24.pdf, PDF page 5, finally passed 4/16/2024) adds only the words 'not at the front of a building' (double-underlined Board amendment) to the closing paragraph. amend_prior_conditions.rule: Every condition imposed in a Conditional Use (or other administrative action under the Code) is a requirement of the Code (§ 174), and changing any condition previously imposed in a Conditional Use authorization goes through the same procedure as a new Conditional Use, that is, a new application and Planning Commission hearing (§ 303(e)). So a proposal that exceeds a limit written into a prior motion at the address (hours, amplified sound, floor area, kind of entertainment) needs a new Conditional Use even where the use itself is otherwise allowed.

amend_prior_conditions.note: § 303(e): the archived amlegal copy of 19 Jan 2022 (https://web.archive.org/web/20220119010738/https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/san_francisco/latest/sf_planning/0-0-0-21892) and the gocodebook.com mirror (2026-08 edition, text as of 2026-09-23) are word for word the same; the section's amendment history shows (e) last amended by Ord. 129-17, Eff. 7/30/2017, and later amendments to § 303 (through Ord. 245-25, Eff. 1/12/2026) list other divisions. § 174 was read only on the mirror (no archived capture of its page was found); its history is 'Added by Ord. 443-78, App. 10/6/78' with no amendment. nighttime_entertainment_definition.rule: Nighttime Entertainment (§ 102, 'Entertainment, Nighttime') is a Retail Entertainment, Arts and Recreation Use that includes dance halls, discotheques, nightclubs, private clubs and similar evening-oriented entertainment that requires a dance hall keeper police permit or a Place of Entertainment police permit (Police Code § 1060), not limited to non-amplified live entertainment, and it includes Restaurants and Bars that present such activities. It does not include an Arts Activity, a theater performance space that does not serve alcohol during performances, or temporary uses under §§ 205 et seq. The definition ends: 'This use is also subject to the controls in Section 202.11' (the former § 202.11, a temporary Conditional Use requirement for changing or demolishing a Nighttime Entertainment use). General Entertainment (§ 102, 'Entertainment, General') is entertainment or leisure for the general public inside an enclosed, soundproofed building: dramatic and musical performances where alcohol is not served during performances, arcades with eleven or more amusement game devices, billiard halls, bowling alleys, skating rinks and mini-golf. A Limited Live Performance permit is different: § 102 calls Limited Live Performance 'An Accessory Use as defined in Section 1060 of the Police Code', and under Police Code § 1060 it is a permit for a locale where live performance is a secondary purpose, the performance area is no greater than 200 square feet (indoors, or in an outdoor plaza, courtyard or similar space enclosed by surrounding buildings; larger in a listed Plaza or People Place), and performances end by 11 p.m. (10 p.m. in the North Beach NCD, the Polk Street NCD, and on listed blocks of Chestnut and Lombard Streets). It is not a Place of Entertainment permit, so a venue holding only a Limited Live Performance permit does not, on that fact alone, fall within the Nighttime Entertainment definition.
nighttime_entertainment_definition.kind_note: A definition, not a control. The Historic Building rule recorded in the last version (new § 202.11) is a control that changes which approval is required; it is carried here because the first reader placed it here.

General Entertainment in this period: read as unamended existing text in Ord. 70-23 (PDF page 4), ending '...regulated in Sections 1036 through 1036.24 of the Police Code.' Former § 202.11 ('Temporary limitation on change in use or demolition of Nighttime Entertainment use', added by Ord. 111-21, Eff. 9/4/2021; 'expired 9/4/2024' per the publisher's note; amended by Ord. 33-24, Eff. 3/23/2024, not read) required a Conditional Use for a change in use or demolition of a Nighttime Entertainment use for three years; that is the 'Section 202.11' the definition pointed to until 3/15/2026. It is a rule about removing the use, not about what the use is. Police Code § 1060 was read only in the Internet Archive's single capture of 11 Dec 2024 (history ending Ord. 237-24, Eff. 11/11/2024; earlier amendments in the period: Ord. 96-23, Eff. 6/26/2023, and Ord. 250-23, Eff. 1/14/2024). Its wording on other dates, including the Limited Live Performance hours and area limits in 2022 and after November 2024, was NOT read; the Limited Live Performance sentence in the rule describes the December 2024 text. Police Code § 1060.1 (capture of 20 May 2023) requires a permit to operate a Place of Entertainment or a Limited Live Performance Locale, and § 1060.1(e) exempts a Limited Live Performance Locale where entertainment ends by 10 p.m. and is a single unamplified performer. Zoning Administrator Interpretation 102 (11/91): non-amplified music is not classified as nighttime entertainment. The conclusion that a Limited-Live-Performance-only venue is outside the definition is my reading of the two codes together, not a sentence in either. nighttime_entertainment_definition.rule: Nighttime Entertainment (§ 102, 'Entertainment, Nighttime') is a Retail Entertainment, Arts and Recreation Use that includes dance halls, discotheques, nightclubs, private clubs and similar evening-oriented entertainment that requires a dance hall keeper police permit or a Place of Entertainment police permit (Police Code § 1060), not limited to non-amplified live entertainment, and it includes Restaurants and Bars that present such activities. It does not include an Arts Activity, a theater performance space that does not serve alcohol during performances, or temporary uses under §§ 205 et seq. From this date the definition adds: the use may include a non-profit theater with ABC licence Type 64 and a music entertainment facility with ABC licence Type 90. It still says the use is subject to (former) § 202.11, which expired on 9/4/2024. General Entertainment (§ 102, 'Entertainment, General') is entertainment or leisure for the general public inside an enclosed, soundproofed building: dramatic and musical performances where alcohol is not served during performances, arcades with eleven or more amusement game devices, billiard halls, bowling alleys, skating rinks and mini-golf. From this date General Entertainment may also include a non-profit theater with a Type 64 licence and a music entertainment facility with a Type 90 licence, provided alcohol is not served during performances. A Limited Live Performance permit is different: § 102 calls Limited Live Performance 'An Accessory Use as defined in Section 1060 of the Police Code', and under Police Code § 1060 it is a permit for a locale where live performance is a secondary purpose, the performance area is no greater than 200 square feet (larger in listed plazas and Shared Spaces), and performances end by 11 p.m. (10 p.m. in the North Beach NCD and on listed blocks of Chestnut and Lombard Streets). It is not a Place of Entertainment permit, so a venue holding only a Limited Live Performance permit does not, on that fact alone, fall within the Nighttime Entertainment definition.
nighttime_entertainment_definition.kind_note: A definition, not a control. The Historic Building rule recorded in the last version (new § 202.11) is a control that changes which approval is required; it is carried here because the first reader placed it here.
nighttime_entertainment_definition.section: 102 (Entertainment, Nighttime; Entertainment, General; Limited Live Performance); Police Code 1060, 1060.1; former 202.11
nighttime_entertainment_definition.quote: The use may include a non-profit theater with ABC license Type 64 and a music entertainment facility with ABC license Type 90.
nighttime_entertainment_definition.note: Ord. 249-23 (read at https://sfbos.archive.sf.gov/sites/default/files/o0249-23.pdf, PDF pages 3-4, finally passed 12/12/2023; additions checked on the page images) adds the Type 64 / Type 90 sentence to Nighttime Entertainment and the matching sentence to General Entertainment, and nothing else in either definition. The quote is today's mirror text of the sentence added then. Former § 202.11 ('Temporary limitation on change in use or demolition of Nighttime Entertainment use', added by Ord. 111-21, Eff. 9/4/2021; 'expired 9/4/2024' per the publisher's note; amended by Ord. 33-24, Eff. 3/23/2024, not read) required a Conditional Use for a change in use or demolition of a Nighttime Entertainment use for three years; that is the 'Section 202.11' the definition pointed to until 3/15/2026. It is a rule about removing the use, not about what the use is. Inside this period the former § 202.11 Conditional Use requirement for removing a Nighttime Entertainment use ended (9/4/2024 per the publisher's note); the definition's cross-reference to it stayed until Ord. 13-26. Police Code § 1060 was read only in the Internet Archive's single capture of 11 Dec 2024 (history ending Ord. 237-24, Eff. 11/11/2024; earlier amendments in the period: Ord. 96-23, Eff. 6/26/2023, and Ord. 250-23, Eff. 1/14/2024). Its wording on other dates, including the Limited Live Performance hours and area limits in 2022 and after November 2024, was NOT read; the Limited Live Performance sentence in the rule describes the December 2024 text. Police Code § 1060.1 (capture of 20 May 2023) requires a permit to operate a Place of Entertainment or a Limited Live Performance Locale, and § 1060.1(e) exempts a Limited Live Performance Locale where entertainment ends by 10 p.m. and is a single unamplified performer. Zoning Administrator Interpretation 102 (11/91): non-amplified music is not classified as nighttime entertainment. The conclusion that a Limited-Live-Performance-only venue is outside the definition is my reading of the two codes together, not a sentence in either.

use_definitions.rule: Bar (§ 102): a Retail Sales and Service Use that provides on-site alcoholic beverage sales for drinking on the premises: bars serving beer, wine and/or liquor where no one under 21 is admitted (ABC licence types 23, 42, 48 or 61), drinking establishments serving beer where minors are present (types 40 or 60) in conjunction with other uses such as Movie Theaters and General Entertainment, and bars serving wine operated by licensed winegrowers (type 02). A non-profit theater selling alcohol only to ticket-holding patrons with a type 64 licence is not a Bar. There is no mention of a type 90 licence. Restaurant (§ 102): serves prepared, ready-to-eat cooked foods for consumption on the premises and has seating; it may provide on-site beer, wine and/or liquor sales for drinking on the premises with ABC licence types 02, 23, 41, 47, 49, 59, 75 or 87, and if it does it must operate as a Bona Fide Eating Place. Limited Restaurant (§ 102, 'Restaurant, Limited'): serves ready-to-eat foods and/or drinks for consumption on or off the premises, with or without seating; it shall not provide on-site beer and/or wine sales for consumption on the premises, but may sell beer and/or wine for off-premises consumption with a type 20 licence if the display and sale area is less than 15% of the Occupied Floor Area. The Limited Restaurant definition also says that within the North Beach SUD it is distinct from Specialty Food Manufacturing (§ 780.3(b)).

neighbourhood_notification.rule: Building permit applications in Residential, NC, NCT and Eastern Neighborhoods Mixed Use districts for a change of use (and for establishing a Formula Retail use) are subject to § 311 neighbourhood notification (mailed and posted notice, 30-day hold). In Residential, NC and NCT districts a 'change of use' means a change to, or addition of, any of the listed uses, which include Bar, General Entertainment, Limited Restaurant, Liquor Store, Nighttime Entertainment, Outdoor Activity Area and Restaurant (Restaurant to Limited-Restaurant is exempt); in Eastern Neighborhoods Mixed Use districts it means a change in, or addition of, a land use category. Exemption adopted by the voters in November 2020 (Proposition H, Eff. 12/18/2020): a change of use to a principally permitted use in an NC or NCT district, or in a limited commercial use or limited corner commercial use (§§ 186, 231), is not subject to § 311 review or notice. So in an NC or NCT district notice attaches only where the new use is not principally permitted (and a use needing a Conditional Use gets its hearing notice instead; § 311(d)(6) allows the duplicate notice to be waived). Districts outside that list (for example C-2 and C-3) are not covered by § 311.
neighbourhood_notification.kind_note: Neighbourhood notification is a notice step inside a building permit, not an approval of its own and not an agency referral. Under spec section 3a it is treated like a referral step: it never sets a row's status, and its removal for changes of use on 2024-01-14 removed no approval (the building permit and any Conditional Use are still required).

change_of_occupancy.rule: A restaurant, bar, tavern or nightclub is an Assembly Group A-2 occupancy (assembly uses intended for food and/or drink consumption) (§ 303.3), but a building or tenant space used for assembly purposes with an occupant load of less than 50 persons is classified as Group B (§ 303.1.1). So the line is 50 occupants: 49 or fewer is Group B, 50 or more is A-2. (2019 California Building Code.) In San Francisco, whenever a change in occupancy or use is made, a building permit is required to legalize it, and it must be secured before the change of occupancy; where alteration work is required, the alteration permit is sufficient and no further permit is needed for the change (San Francisco Building Code § 106A.1.12).
change_of_occupancy.section: California Building Code 2019 edition, § 303.1.1, § 303.3; San Francisco Building Code § 106A.1.12

Edition dates from the Building Standards Commission page: the 2019 edition had 'an effective date of January 1, 2020' and the 2022 edition 'an effective date of January 1, 2023', so this version ends 2022-12-31. San Francisco Building Code § 106A.1.12: no copy dated in this period was read. The sentence is taken as in force throughout because it reads the same in an earlier published amlegal version of Section 106A (latest history date Eff. 5/13/2019) and as unchanged base text in Ord. 241-24 of October 2024; nothing read shows an amendment in between, but the section carries no history note. Not read: how the occupant load is computed (Chapter 10, Table 1004.5); San Francisco's local amendments, if any, to Chapter 3 of this edition (the 2025 edition has none); San Francisco's ordinance adopting this edition. The existing occupancy group of a space is not in public records.

change_of_occupancy.rule: A restaurant, bar, tavern or nightclub is an Assembly Group A-2 occupancy (assembly uses intended for food and/or drink consumption) (§ 303.3), but a building or tenant space used for assembly purposes with an occupant load of less than 50 persons is classified as Group B (§ 303.1.1). So the line is 50 occupants: 49 or fewer is Group B, 50 or more is A-2. (2022 California Building Code.) In San Francisco, whenever a change in occupancy or use, as defined in Building Code § 302, is made, a building permit is required to legalize it, and it must be secured before the change of occupancy; where alteration work is required, the alteration permit with plans is sufficient (San Francisco Building Code § 106A.1.12). From this date a building permit application for a change of use needs no plans by a registered design professional if the use stays within the A, B or M classification, the occupant load does not rise, there are no alterations, no mechanical, electrical or plumbing changes and no new kitchen or service bar (§ 106A.1.12(a)-(e)); the permit itself is still required.

over_concentration.rule: For an original licence or a premises-to-premises transfer of any retail licence, 'undue concentration' exists where (1) the premises are in a crime reporting district with 20 percent more reported crimes than the average of the local agency's reporting districts, or (2) for an on-sale licence, the ratio of on-sale retail licences to population in the census tract (or census division) exceeds the ratio for the county, or (3) the same for off-sale licences (§ 23958.4(a)). The licence may still issue: (b)(1) for a nonretail licence, a retail on-sale bona fide eating place licence, a hotel/motel/lodging licence, a retail licence issued with a beer manufacturer's licence, or a winegrower's licence, if the applicant shows the Department that public convenience or necessity would be served; (b)(2) for any other licence (for example a bar or an off-sale licence), if the local governing body, or the officer or body it designates, determines within 90 days of notice of a completed application that public convenience or necessity would be served; if it makes no determination in 90 days, the Department may issue on the applicant's showing. The section does not apply if the premises have been licensed and operated with the same type of licence within 90 days of the application (§ 23958.4(f)). Over-concentration is therefore a further-review fact, never a bar on its own. Separately, no retail licence may be issued for premises where exercising the licence is contrary to a valid zoning ordinance (§ 23790): where the Planning Code prohibits the use, the licence cannot issue.
over_concentration.kind_note: Undue concentration is a finding inside the ABC licence application, not a separate approval. Where it exists, a public convenience or necessity showing or local determination is an extra step within the licence; the licence itself is the approval. Treated like a referral step under spec section 3a.
over_concentration.quote: As to on-sale retail license applications, the ratio of on-sale retail licenses to population in the census tract or census division in which the applicant premises are located exceeds the ratio of on-sale retail licenses to population in the county in which the applicant premises are located.

The statute does not list ABC type numbers in (b); which numbered types are 'bona fide eating place' licences (the restaurant types) and which fall under 'any other license' (bars, off-sale) is my reading. entertainment_permits.rule: A One Time Event Permit is required to hold a One-Time Event (an event for a group of people at which Entertainment is furnished, not at a private residence). The Entertainment Commission's Director issues it without a Commission hearing, except that a hearing is held where events have occurred at the premises on 12 or more days within the previous 12-month period, unless the Commission or Director finds a hearing unnecessary.

entertainment_permits.quote: At any premises where events have occurred for a total of 12 or more days within the previous 12-month period, upon receipt of a permit application for a One Time Event Permit, the Entertainment Commission, or its Director as delegated by the Entertainment Commission, shall hold a hearing on the permit application

sources.quote: “One Time Event.” An indoor event, or outdoor event such as a concert, parade, fair, festival, athletic event, or block party, that is organized for a group of people, (a) at which Entertainment is furnished or occurs, and (b) which takes place at any location in the City that is not a Private Residence.

entertainment_permits.rule: A dance permit from the Entertainment Commission was required to operate a dance hall or to conduct, promote or sponsor a dance, unless the location held a valid Place of Entertainment Permit; invitation-only social dances with no fee, and certain agency, nonprofit and dance-class dances, were outside the rules. ordinance_118_25.summary: Ordinance No. 118-25 (File No. 250537, 'Police Code - Entertainment Permits', sponsors Mayor Lurie and Supervisors Sherrill and Sauter) exists and was read in full as published by the Board of Supervisors (23 scanned pages; the pages with strike-outs and the signature page were read as images). It passed first reading on 8 July 2025, was finally passed on 15 July 2025 (11 ayes) and was approved by the Mayor on 17 July 2025. Its own text says only that it takes effect 30 days after enactment. The Police Code's cover page and the Board's ordinance index give 17 August 2025; the City's PermitSF page gives 16 August 2025, one day earlier. This file uses 17 August 2025, so every removed step has 'to' 2025-08-16. Referrals removed: the Department of Building Inspection referral for Place of Entertainment Permits (§ 1060.2(b)(3)) and for Extended-Hours Premises Permits (§ 1070.2(b)); the Planning Department referral for Limited Live Performance Permits (§ 1060.2.1(b)) and Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound Permits (§ 1060.2.2(b)). Referrals narrowed: for Extended-Hours Premises Permits, no referral to the Department of Public Health or the Fire Department where the applicant already holds that department's current permit. All four permits are still required, and the Planning referral for Place of Entertainment and Extended-Hours Premises Permits stays. Permits eliminated outright: ball or ring throwing game permits (§ 1021) and dance hall and dance permits (§§ 1022 to 1027). The title also names masked ball permits, but § 1029 had already been deleted by Ord. 250-23 in January 2024. Other changes: a flat $558 filing fee for One Time Outdoor Amplified Sound Permits (§ 2.26); notice rules for Place of Entertainment, Limited Live Performance and Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound applications relaxed (§§ 1060.5, 1060.5.1, 1060.5.2); the 12-day hearing trigger for One Time Event and One Time Outdoor Amplified Sound Permits counted by calendar year instead of the previous 12 months (§§ 1060.29, 1060.29.2); a fee-waiver clarification (§ 1060.19); noise definitions (§ 2901). Also relevant and not in the spec: Ord. 250-23 had earlier removed the Department of Public Health referral for Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound Permits and widened the exception to the Building Inspection referral for Place of Entertainment Permits.
